The answer to the oath is: ﴿What you are promised is true, and indeed the Recompense is surely going to occur﴾ [51:5-6].

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, swears: ﴿By the Mount [al-Ṭūr], and by a Book inscribed, in parchment unrolled, and by the much-frequented House, and by the raised canopy, and by the surging sea﴾ [52:1-6]. The answer to the oath is: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur, there is none to avert it﴾ [52:7-8]. When we consider the things sworn by in the two places, we find that in al-Dhariyat He swore by material things: He swore by the winds and the clouds that carry the water that gives life to the earth.

On the Day of Judgment, the sky will be violently shaken: "On the Day when the sky will sway violently." Now, the good of the Causer is received only by those who believed in Him and affirmed His messengers during the time when the causes remained.

Therefore we say: beware of being deceived by causes, no matter how much they obey you and no matter how much they give you, and know that behind the causes is their Causer.

Or: He protected them from the punishment of Hellfire at the outset, before they entered Paradise, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Whoever is spared from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 185].

So it is hani' but not mari' (wholesome in its after-effects). God describes the food and drink of Paradise as hani' and mari': that is, it passes smoothly over you and you find in it no harmful effects.

Even if the food and drink of Paradise contain none of this, because the person there does not eat out of hunger, but eats for enjoyment, and even if he does not eat, it makes no difference.

Then the Exalted mentions other kinds of bliss.

Reclining is a posture of sitting: one does not sit squarely on one's buttocks but sits leaning on one side, and this is a sitting that indicates comfort and tranquility, and that nothing disturbs it.

As for the worried person, God forbid, you find him in his sitting restless, hardly able to lean his back against a support. Why? Because he has something that preoccupies him, even from comfort in sitting.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿reclining﴾ [al-Tur: 20] indicates calmness of mind and its freedom from disturbances and worries. ﴿on couches﴾ [al-Tur: 20]: plural of sarir (couch), which is that on which one sits, and its wording indicates joy. ﴿arranged in rows﴾ [al-Tur: 20]: organized and well-ordered, joined to one another.

Therefore, when we went to France, we saw there hotels extremely splendid, beautiful and comfortable, and people were amazed by them. I said to them: "Are you amazed at this which human beings have prepared for human beings? Then what about what the Lord of human beings has prepared for human beings?"

And the meaning of: ﴿and We will marry them to fair-eyed companions [hur 'in]﴾ [al-Tur: 20], i.e., We will pair them with the hur 'in (wide-eyed, lustrous-eyed maidens). The verb zawwaja (to marry) is transitive by itself; you say zawwajtu fulanan fulanah ("I married so-and-so to such-and-such a woman"), because marriage here is a mutual benefit enjoyed by both husband and wife together.

As for the marriage to the hur 'in, it is a benefit from one side only: the believer in Paradise enjoys marriage to the hawra' (maiden), but as for her, she has no enjoyment in that. Therefore He said ﴿and We will marry them to﴾ [al-Tur: 20], so the verb was transitive by means of the preposition bi (with).

And the meaning of al-hur al-'in: the plural of hawra', who is one whose eye-white is extremely white and whose pupil is extremely black; and al-'in is the plural of 'ayna', who is wide-eyed, in beauty and grace.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 52, verse 21:

﴿And those who believed...﴾ [al-Tur: 21] That is: they believed in God alone, without partner, and that He is One (wahid), the Unique (ahad), and they held that belief. "One" (wahid) means there is nothing with Him other than Him; "Unique" (ahad) means in His essence; "ahad" means He has no parts. ﴿Say: He is God, the One.﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1].

Faith is not complete unless it is accompanied by action in accordance with that faith: action by the method that He Whom you believe in has laid down for you. Therefore, in many places He joins faith with righteous deeds, saying: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds...﴾ [al-Talaq: 11].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And their offspring followed them in faith...﴾ [al-Tur: 21]. The man believed and did righteous deeds, and his offspring after him followed him in this, believing as he believed, but their deeds were less than their father's and fell short of his. So God, exalted is He, out of His generosity and mercy toward the offspring, and as an honour to the believing father, raises his son up to the higher rank.

﴿We will join their offspring to them, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds...﴾ [al-Tur: 21]: We did not diminish them in anything. We added to the children and did not reduce the fathers, because the condition of faith is present in both. As for deeds, if they are few, they are made up by God's grace and generosity.

The meaning of "dhurriyyah" (offspring) is a continuing lineage: the offspring of a man are his children and his children's children. The father is among the offspring, and the son is among the offspring, so lineage is continuous in it. Offspring are of two kinds: offspring before reaching legal responsibility (taklif) and offspring after reaching it. What is meant here is the offspring who are legally responsible, from whom faith and righteous deeds are required. And the phrase ﴿...any of their deeds...﴾ [al-Tur: 21] means: any thing, however small.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾ [al-Tur: 21]. "Rahin" (held in pledge) is an intensive form on the pattern fa'il. This pattern can come with the meaning of the active participle, as in "rahim" meaning "merciful" (rahim, one who shows mercy), and it can come with the meaning of the passive participle, as in "qatil" meaning "killed" (maqtul).

Here "rahin" means "marhun" (pledged), from "rahn" (pledge). The rahn, as you know, is a tangible thing that a person in need of money places with the lender as security for him until he repays his debt. The pledge remains tied to the money until it returns to its owner. Likewise, the servant on the Day of Resurrection is held in pledge by his deed, confined to it.

Or we may say: "rahin" means "rahin" in the active sense: he pledges his deed; if it is good, he finds it good, and if it is evil, he finds it evil.

**The words of the Most High: ﴿And We will increase them﴾ [al-Tur: 22]** — meaning: this is a new bestowal, beyond what came before and added to it. ﴿They will pass around in it﴾ [al-Tur: 23] — that is, in Paradise they pass around the cup, meaning they pull it to one another. This passing-around is not out of dispute or enmity, but out of companionship, gentleness and intimacy, so it is as though they drink in enjoyment, harmony and delicate ease.

﴿They pass around in it a cup﴾ [al-Tur: 23] — the kas (cup) is the vessel from which wine is drunk, and it is not called a kas unless it is full; if it is empty, it is a kub (goblet).

The meaning of ﴿there is no idle talk in it﴾ [al-Tur: 23] — laghw (idle talk): an action that has no benefit in it, namely fallen speech that has no meaning. ﴿Nor any sinfulness﴾ [al-Tur: 23] — there is no sin in it, and it does not draw one toward what is forbidden.

This is the distinguishing feature of the wine of the Hereafter, and the difference between it and the wine of this world: the wine of this world takes away the intellect and drives its drinker to raving and loss of reason, and consequently idle talk arises from him, and sin arises from him.

As for the wine of the Hereafter, it is free of this. For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, described it by His saying: ﴿And rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. So: the Truth, glorified is He, has purified it of its defects; it has of the wine of this world only the name. And if you see the one who drinks wine, you see him spill it out of his mouth at once like this — why? Because it is bitter in taste and foul in smell.

As for the Hereafter, one tastes it and enjoys its pleasure. If the wine of this world is of this description, then why do they drink it? When you ask, he says to you: "So that I may forget my worries, my sorrows and my troubles."

This is strange, for God the Exalted does not want us to forget worries and sorrows and flee from them; rather He wants us to face them, know their causes, and try to overcome them. So there is no benefit in forgetting them and concealing them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 52, verse 28:

He mentions here the reason for their entering Paradise and their salvation from the Fire. The cause is that they were people who made much supplication (du'a'). They did not say, "It is by our deeds," but rather by our supplication, our humble entreaty, and our hope in God. We call upon Him as a Lord who is merciful, a bountiful Benefactor, and we aspire to His mercy, which preceded His wrath.

﴿Indeed, He is the Benefactor, the Merciful﴾ [al-Tur: 28]. So He answered us with an answer whose effects appeared in our entering Paradise and our arriving at something better than what we had been in, without fatigue, worry, or grief. We arrived at a bliss that had never occurred to us.

﴿Al-Barr﴾ [al-Tur: 28] means abundant in generosity and benevolence, and ﴿al-Rahim﴾ [al-Tur: 28] means abundant in mercy toward His creation, exalted is He, because He is their Lord, their Creator, and the One who takes charge of them. He created them from nothing and sustained them from nothing, and He did not impose duties upon them except after puberty and the soundness of intellect, along with other blessings.

This is a command to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he should remind his people. Tadhkir (reminding) means that you repeat what you have been told and restate it many times, and reminding is only needed for forgetfulness, which is the nature of human beings that God created them with.

Reminding benefits in several respects. First, it benefits the one who reminds, because when he repeats the reminder he is not deprived of its reward. Then it benefits the believer who is reminded: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 55].

The events of life pass over the believer, and they may cloud over the clarity of his faith. Reminding removes this cloud and wipes away the dust of heedlessness and forgetfulness.

For this reason, our master Mu'adh used often to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about matters he had missed.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Likewise, reminding is not barred from benefiting the disbeliever, as is shown by the fact that the chieftains of disbelief in Makkah believed through reminding. The essential thing is that the reminder reaches a pure heart, to extinguish in it the zeal of jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance).

We have seen this matter in the story of the conversion of our master 'Umar, who was a tyrant in the jahiliyyah. Yet when he heard the Qur'an, he was affected by it and his heart softened, because when he slapped his sister until blood flowed from her face, the feeling of brotherhood and what it entails of tenderness and softness of heart stirred in him. When his heart opened, the light of guidance entered it and he embraced Islam. So reminding benefited him.

As for His, glorified be He, saying: ﴿So you, by the grace of your Lord, are neither a soothsayer nor a madman﴾ [at-Tur: 29], Almighty Allah negates from His Messenger this accusation with which they charged him, and He emphasised this negation by using the style of address.

In ﴿So you are not...﴾ [at-Tur: 29], and the use of the particle bi (ba') in ﴿a soothsayer...﴾ [at-Tur: 29], it means: there is nothing of soothsaying in you at all. The kahin (soothsayer) is the diviner who claims knowledge of the unseen, and there were many of them at this time.

They had a freakish form, deviating from the normal creation. For example, among them was Shiqq Anmar, who had half an eye, half a nose, half a mouth, half a hand and half a leg.

Such people, the Lord had not granted some purity. The devils used to descend upon them and inspire them with things through eavesdropping before his (ﷺ) mission, before the heaven was closed against them. They would deceive people with things that contained a little truth and much falsehood, which they increased from their own, thereby misguiding them.

These soothsayers had an influential word, and people would consult them and follow their opinion in all matters of their religion and their worldly affairs.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is far removed from this attribute. Likewise, He negated from him the attribute of madness, and the madman is one who has no intellect, cannot arrange things, and cannot direct the movement of his life.

Have you witnessed anything of this in the Messenger of Allah, when he has been known among you for soundness of mind, good conduct, truthfulness and trustworthiness? How could it be, when Allah has praised him, saying: ﴿And indeed, you are of a great moral character﴾ [al-Qalam: 4].

As for His, glorified be He, saying: ﴿So you, by the grace of your Lord...﴾ [at-Tur: 29], meaning: the blessings of Allah upon you are many, and among them is that you are not what he says, neither a soothsayer nor a madman. Or, "remind by the grace of your Lord," not by the grace of a soothsayer or the grace of a madman. Then He negates from him another accusation, saying:

﴿Or do they say, "A poet, for whom we await misfortune..."﴾

They said of the Messenger of Allah, after their stratagems had failed them and they found no echo for their claims that he was a soothsayer (kāhin) and a madman, "a poet" (shā'ir). They did not succeed in this either, for the Messenger of Allah came to a people who were most eloquent. They possess a faculty of rhetoric and precision in linguistic and expressive performance; they are the people most knowledgeable about poetry, and they know that what Muhammad brought, and what he recites to them, is not poetry, and they had never tested him in anything of this kind before his mission.

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said in refuting their claim: ﴿Say: "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it. I lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then use your reason?"﴾ [Yunus: 16].

Where are your thinking minds? I lived among you for forty years, and you never caught me composing poetry. Has poetic genius then burst forth in me after forty? And it is well known that poetic genius (ʿabqariyyāt) comes in the second decade of life.

Moreover, what would guarantee to me that I possess a genius that produces this speech before I die? Then, I do not tell you that this is my own speech.

Rather, it is from Allah, by revelation from Allah, which is not given to a soothsayer, for the soothsayer only receives from the devils: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies...﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. Nor is it given to a madman, nor to a sorcerer, nor to a poet.

When they failed in this too, they said: ﴿The fables of the ancients﴾ [al-Qalam: 15]. And they said: "Muhammad is taking lessons from a man of the People of the Book who teaches him this speech." But the Qur'an exposed them, clarified their lie and the contradictions in their statements, and Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [al-Nahl: 103].

Indeed, all this is obstinacy and contentiousness in dispute, which does not stand before a sensible, reflective person.

The meaning of ﴿we await for him misfortune of time﴾ [al-Tur: 30] is: we wait for what befalls him of the events of life and the sudden coming of death, from which he will give us rest. So Allah answered them: ﴿Say, "Wait, for I am with you among those who wait."﴾ [al-Tur: 31].

Here the command ﴿Say, "Wait..."﴾ [al-Tur: 31] is a command of threat, as you say to your opponent, "Ride whatever horse you have," meaning: do whatever you wish; the meaning is, however much you do, you will not gain anything from me.

So Allah says to them: wait as you wish; you will not gain anything from us, nor will you plot against us, for we are under the care of Allah and within the sight of Allah.

It has already been tested: you harmed us with words and gained nothing from us; you harmed us with action and we did not abandon our message; you harmed us with deceit and plotting to kill us, so Allah turned your plotting back upon your own necks. When you did not succeed in open plotting, you turned to hidden plotting and sought help against us from the jinn and the sorcerers, but you did not reach your aim, and Allah frustrated your effort.

So then: wait as you wish, and know that we too are waiting for you. Allah, the Exalted, explained this matter in another verse, saying: ﴿Say, "Do you await for us except one of the two best outcomes? And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Himself, or by our hands. So wait; indeed we are waiting with you."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 52].

And we await concerning you: either that Allah punish you in the Hereafter for your disbelief, or that He punish you by our hands when we triumph over you. So wait concerning us; you will reach no plotting against us at all, for we are under the care of Allah and within the sight of Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 52, verse 32:

The meaning of "al-aḥlām" (intellects, minds): the intellects. When the intellects command them, ﴿with this﴾, i.e., with this obstinacy and clashing against the call of Allah, this is evidence of the corruption of these intellects and the corruption of this thinking, because if the intellects were left to the innate nature (fitrah) upon which they were created, and if they were freed from desires, they would end only in faith in Allah and His Messenger, and would not have taken this stance.

﴿Or are they a people transgressing?﴾ Allah, glorified and exalted, repeated "am" (or) here in several places to present all the positions and possibilities they went through. The meaning of ﴿transgressing﴾ is: going beyond the limit in disbelief, in obstinacy, and in clashing against the call.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 52, verses 33–34:

﴿He has fabricated it﴾ [al-Tur: 33]: he invented it and brought it from himself. When this slander did not take hold, they said: ﴿It is only a human being who teaches him﴾ [al-Nahl: 103], and Allah answered them: ﴿The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Nahl: 103].

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, responds to them: ﴿Rather, they do not believe﴾ [al-Tur: 33]. That is, the matter is not one of a Qur'an from Muhammad; the matter is that they do not wish to enter the courtyard of faith. Thus, out of injustice, obstinacy and arrogance, they turn away from accepting the truth without reflection, without consideration or thought.

All these accusations they tried to attach to the Messenger of Allah or to his Book, they know to be falsehood, which they brought from themselves in order to divert Muhammad from his call, while they know that he is truthful, that the Qur'an is true, and that it is from Allah. But they do not want to believe.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches them the manner of sound reflection that leads to the truth, and says to them: ﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing: that you stand up for Allah, in pairs and individually, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion﴾ [Saba': 46].

That is: abandon collective thinking and mass talk, for it does not lead to the truth.

So: if you reflect and employ your minds in a correct way, you will surely arrive at a reality, namely that Muhammad is truthful in what he has brought you.

The Qur'an calls them to reflection only when that reflection will lead them to this reality. Therefore we often read ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 68], ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ [Yunus: 3], ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ [al-An'am: 50].

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it, if they are truthful﴾ [al-Tur: 34]: that is, if the Qur'an is fabricated as they claim, then let them produce a Qur'an like it, fabricated in the same way. They are the most capable of people in speech and expression, and the most eloquent of people, and they have markets for oratory and poetry. ﴿If they are truthful﴾ [al-Tur: 34]: that is, in this claim.

Therefore He asks: ﴿Were they created from nothing?﴾ [al-Tur: 35] How could they be, when creation (al-khalq) is bringing into existence from non-existence? Did they come into the universe in this way, without a Creator? Reason says that nothing can come into existence except by an originator, even in the most trivial things.

In this cup from which we are drinking now, a transparent crystal cup, after we used to drink from tin or earthenware, is it reasonable for us to say that this cup came into being in this way, without an originator? Therefore: this creation must have a Creator.

Then he moves on to another aspect of the question of creation: ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ [al-Tur: 35], that is, the creators of this creation. In another place Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87]

Yes, they cannot say anything other than this, because man came into a wondrous universe in which there are sun, moon, stars, earth, water, air, sky and mountains. How, then, can he say, "I am the one who created it," when it is older than him? He cannot even say, "I created myself." And if he said it, then who created your father, and who traced the chain back until it reaches Adam, peace be upon him?

Therefore: this logical sequence must lead us to a Creator who created and was not created, namely Almighty Allah.

For this reason He said after it: ﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they do not have certainty.﴾ [al-Tur: 36] If they cannot create themselves, then they certainly did not create the heavens and the earth, by a fortiori reasoning.

We have already said that this matter of creation has not been claimed by anyone for himself, and the claim stands for whoever makes it until someone appears to contest it; and no one has said that he created the heavens and the earth.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 52, verse 37:

Meaning: Do they own the treasuries of provision, so that they give provision to whom they wish and withhold it from whom they wish, or do they own the treasuries of mercy, so that they show mercy to whom they wish? ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ [al-Tur: 37] — the masters of authority, of dominance, of command and prohibition, and of supremacy.

The answer: neither this nor that. For God Most High alone withheld the rain from them, so they went hungry, until they ate the leaves of trees, the 'ilhiz, which is blood mixed with camel hair. Then they went to seek rain through the intercession of the uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ).

They acknowledged that the treasuries are the treasuries of God, and that they have no share in the affair at all. The proof is that they are sometimes rich and sometimes poor, sometimes strong and sometimes weak.

So, they have no treasuries of anything: the treasuries are with the One whom you dislike and deny. Likewise, they have no dominance or control over the reins of the cosmos or the management of affairs. The proof is that the small believing group defeated them despite their numbers on the day of Badr, and captured their chieftains, and they came negotiating with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) so that he would accept ransom for them.

He says to them: "Do you have a ladder?" ﴿Sullam﴾ means a means of ascent by which you climb to the heavens and then bring the like of what Muhammad brought. So this is an admission from you that there is something in the heavens, but you lack the ladder by which to climb to it. The one who has no ladder is the one to whom revelation came from heaven.

﴿So let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ means: if they have a listener, let him bring a clear proof by which he overcomes Muhammad.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Or has He daughters while you have sons?﴾ This verse exposes the foolishness of the people regarding daughters. They used to despise females and prefer males.

The Qur'an recorded this about them in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When one of them is given news of a female, his face becomes darkened and he is filled with suppressed grief. He hides himself from the people because of the ill of what he has been given news of. Shall he keep it despite humiliation, or bury it in the dust?﴾

He also mentioned their burying of daughters, saying: ﴿When the buried girl is asked, for what sin was she killed?﴾ Then they attributed to God the lesser and to themselves the higher. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be written down and they will be questioned.﴾

In another place, the Truth, glorified is He, shows their transgression in this matter, saying: ﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him? That would be an unjust division.﴾ That is, a division that is unfair and oppressive. How can God, the Creator, have the lesser sex while you have the higher sex?

The verses are still asking about the reason these people turn away and deny the path of truth. Did the Messenger ask them for a wage for his call to them, so that it weighed heavily on them and they were unable to pay it?

Al-maghram (the burdensome debt, i.e., a payment exacted without any crime or right) is money paid without any offence or lawful claim. The meaning of ﴿مُّثْقَلُونَ﴾ [al-Tur: 40] is "burdened," i.e., exhausted and unable to bear it.

The Qur'an has recorded in several places that the messengers did not ask for a wage for their call to people, and that their reward for this is with Allah who sent them. Allah the Most High says: ﴿So whatever wage I have asked of you, it is not but upon Allah...﴾ [Yunus: 72].

Or have they looked into the unseen and found that they will be lords in the Hereafter as they were lords in this world, and that their Hereafter will be better than their worldly life, like the one who said: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a final destination﴾ [al-Kahf: 36]. The meaning is: your call, O Muhammad, does not concern them in anything, for they will enter Paradise in any case and by whatever way!!

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 52, verse 42:

That is: they intend a plot against you. Kayd (plotting) is scheming and devising in secret to inflict harm upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The danger of kayd is that it is planned in secrecy, so you do not see it in order to confront it. For this reason it is the habit of the weak and powerless who cannot face their enemy openly.

And when such a person seizes an opportunity, he does not waste it, as the poet said:

"A weak one, when she gets an opportunity, kills; and that is the nature of the weak."

As for His words, glorified is He: ﴿So those who disbelieve...﴾ [al-Tur: 42], the people of plotting and scheming, ﴿they are the ones who will be plotted against﴾ [al-Tur: 42], as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own people...﴾ [Fatir: 43]. This is because when they plot, they conceal their scheme from people like themselves; but when Allah plots against them, no one can repel that plot. So His plotting against the disbelievers is painful and severe.

The meaning of ﴿they are the ones who will be plotted against﴾ [al-Tur: 42] is: the plot falls upon them, so the word is a passive participle (ism maf'ul).

The proof that Allah frustrated their efforts is that He nullified their plot against the Messenger of Allah. Indeed, He made their plot turn back upon them. They plotted against the Messenger of Allah on the night of the Hijrah, and they agreed to kill him and conspired against him, so that his blood would be divided among the tribes. Yet despite that scheming and devising, they were mocked and had dust thrown on their heads, while he escaped and was not harmed.

This is another question: what has turned them away from the call of God? Is there a god other than God, the true God? And if there were, where is he in the matter of the creation of the heavens and the earth? Why was he silent and did not respond?

The Exalted, Glorified, discusses this matter with them and says: ﴿Had there been other gods with Him, as they claim, they would surely have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne﴾ [al-Isra: 42].

Then the second half of the verse comes to clarify the question at its beginning. ﴿Glory be to Allah...﴾ [al-Tur: 43], exalted and far removed ﴿above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Tur: 43] and above what they claim, because Allah is One, the Unique, the Single, the Eternal Refuge, who has no offspring and no partner, and ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 52, verse 44:

﴿Kisfan...﴾ [al-Tur: 44] is the plural of kisfa, meaning a large piece of cloud. The meaning of ﴿Markum﴾ [al-Tur: 44] is: some of it piled upon some other, as the Exalted said in another place: ﴿Then He makes it into layers, and you see the rain coming out from within it...﴾ [al-Nur: 43].

Look how cosmic phenomena deceive them: they think them a blessing, but they turn out to be a punishment and a torment. When they see pieces of cloud passing over them, they think they carry rain and goodness, but they fall upon them as a torment.

This meaning is clear in His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud that will give us rain."...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 24], meaning: a cloud that will water us. ﴿Rather, it is that which you were impatient for: a wind in which is a painful punishment. * Destroying everything by the command of its Lord, so they became not seen except their dwellings...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 24-25].

And here the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿So leave them until they meet...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 52, verses 45–46:

﴿So leave them...﴾ [al-Tur: 45] Leave them and let them be. The meaning is that there is no benefit from them and no hope in them. So leave them, and do not burden yourself, in the cause of guiding them, with what you cannot bear. Indeed, his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message)...﴾ [al-Nahl: 82].

So then: leave them ﴿until they meet their Day in which they will be struck senseless﴾ [al-Tur: 45], i.e., the thunderbolt and destruction will befall them, and the intended day is the Day of Resurrection. Then this day is further explained, saying: ﴿the Day when their plotting will avail them nothing at all...﴾ [al-Tur: 46], i.e., their scheming against the Messenger of Allah and their conspiring against him.

﴿Nor will they be helped﴾ [al-Tur: 46]: they will have no helper from Allah and no one to ward off the punishment from them, because the affair belongs to Allah alone on that day.

The intended referents here are the disbelievers of Makkah, because they wronged themselves by disbelief and deprived themselves of a blessing that would last in the Hereafter had they believed, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ [an-Nahl: 118]. For these there is ﴿a punishment short of that...﴾ [at-Tur: 47], meaning that before the punishment of the Hereafter, punishment will overtake them in this world. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ [at-Tur: 47].

This is a command to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to be patient with the decree and judgment of Allah. It is a command accompanied by this care and this attention, which were bestowed exclusively upon our master, the Messenger of Allah, and our master Noah, peace be upon them both. His Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Build the ark under Our eyes and Our inspiration...﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 27].

So the Exalted One consoles His Messenger (ﷺ) and reassures him: Be patient, O Muhammad, over the harm of the people, for you are under Our gaze, in Our care and protection, so do not worry about what they do.

This station was also granted specially to our master Moses, peace be upon him, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and that you may be brought up under My eye﴾ [Ta-Ha: 39].

So, His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you are under Our eyes...﴾ [al-Tur: 48] is a higher rank that befits the station of the master of the prophets, Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And glorify your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ [al-Tur: 48], meaning: glorify Him with glorification joined with praise. ﴿When you arise﴾ [al-Tur: 48], meaning: when you rise from your gathering, say: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Allah." This is an expiation for whatever may have occurred in your gathering, and a purification of the gathering and its conclusion. Or ﴿when you arise﴾ [al-Tur: 48], meaning: when you rise from your sleep, so you glorify Allah and praise Him for restoring your soul to you and restoring your vigour to you after sleep. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us to say upon rising: , and to recite Surat al-'Asr upon rising from a gathering, for it is an expiation for what occurred in it.

Likewise, ﴿And during the night, glorify Him...﴾ [al-Tur: 49], meaning: glorify your Lord during the hours of the night, at its beginning and at its end. ﴿And at the retreat of the stars﴾ [al-Tur: 49], meaning: at the time of the pre-dawn (sahar) when the stars set. The meaning is: glorify your Lord at all these times, so that it is a continuous glorification, because Allah has bestowed favours upon you and singled you out with blessings that warrant this glorification and this praise.
